title: "Quiz: The terminal"
---

[Lecture](../lectures/03-terminal/lec.qmd) · [Exercises](03-terminal.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** You are in `route-challenge/results/notes`. The folder `inputs` is directly
inside `route-challenge`. Which command reaches it?

(i) `cd ../inputs`  (ii) `cd ../../inputs`  (iii) `cd inputs`

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Draw the route back to the folder containing both `results` and `inputs`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). The first `..` reaches `results`; the second reaches `route-challenge`.
From there, enter `inputs`.
:::

---

**Q2.** What differs between `mkdir field notes` and `mkdir "field notes"`?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
How many destination arguments does the shell read in each command?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The first creates two directories, `field` and `notes`. The second creates one
directory whose name contains a space: `field notes`.
:::

---

**Q3.** A terminal is in `practice`. You run `cd missing-folder`, and the shell
reports that the folder does not exist. What does `pwd` show afterwards?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Did the requested change of directory succeed?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The path to `practice`. A failed `cd` leaves the current working directory
unchanged. Use `ls` to inspect the names that actually exist.
:::

---

**Q4.** Two terminal windows are in the same directory. In the first, you run
`cd seedlings`. Does the second window move too? Have any files moved?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Distinguish a shell's current location from the stored folder tree.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Each shell has its own working directory, so the second stays where it was.
`cd` changes a shell's location; it moves no files or folders.
:::

---

**Q5.** Which command creates a directory: `pwd`, `ls`, `mkdir readings`, or
`cd readings`? What do the other three do?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which commands inspect storage, and which change a location?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
`mkdir readings` creates the directory. `pwd` prints the current directory;
`ls` lists its entries; `cd readings` enters an existing directory.
:::
